model: Easy UPS 3-Phase with Network Management Card AP9547 (BACnet IP)
applies_to: APC / Schneider Electric Easy UPS 3-Phase units fitted with the Network Management Card for Easy UPS (AP9547), on BACnet IP.
summary: The AP9547 network card puts an Easy UPS 3-Phase on BACnet IP. It exposes 60 read-only Analog Values (runtime, battery, input, bypass and output voltages, currents, power, load percent, maintenance and running-time counters), 60 alarm Binary Values that also send event notifications, five text values (model, serial, firmware) and three Multi-State Values (UPS state, last transfer cause, last battery test).
notes: All objects are read-only in this map; there are no BACnet commands.
Alarm BVs send notifications to the recipients in the Notification Class object (NC 0) set up on the card.
Some bypass objects are not available on every UPS model.
Several names are printed with typos (e.g. OutputApparantPowerL1, OverlaodOnBypassStaticSwitch, BateryCondtionIsWeak); they are kept as printed.
AV 49 BatteryRunningTime and AV 58 AirFilterRunningTime carry copied descriptions in the map (air filter / aux power supply).
Source: BACnet Application Map for Network Management Card for Easy UPS, 3-Phase, 990-6445B (04/2024).

source.title: BACnet Application Map for Network Management Card for Easy UPS, 3-Phase

integration.summary: Enable BACnet on the NMC (see the NMC for Easy UPS user guide), give it a device instance, then read UPS state, runtime, battery charge, load and the key alarm BVs. Use the notification class for alarm events if the BMS supports them.

minimum_points.name: UPSState
minimum_points.why: UPS status: online, on battery, bypass, fault...

minimum_points.name: Runtime
minimum_points.why: Battery runtime left at present load, s

minimum_points.name: OnBattery2
minimum_points.why: UPS on battery after an input problem

minimum_points.name: LowBattery
minimum_points.why: Battery too low to keep supporting the load

minimum_points.name: LostUPSComm
minimum_points.why: Card lost communication with the UPS

integration.enable: BACnet is enabled and configured on the network management card (web interface); there is no BMS enable point.
setup: BACnet settings (enable, device instance, port, BBMD) are on the NMC; see the NMC for Easy UPS user guide.
gotchas: Map is read-only; UPS control is not available over BACnet.
Check BV 0 LostUPSComm before trusting other values.
